evidence.intree_statement: Program Definition Adjunction_from_Transform (A : F ∹ U) : F ⊣ U := {| adj := fun a b => {| to := {| morphism := fun f => fmap f ∘ transform[unit[A]] a |} ; from := {| morphism := fun f => transform[counit[A]] b ∘ fmap f |} |} |}.  — direction (b) ⇒ (a): from a unit η and counit ε the transposes ⌊f⌋ = U f ∘ η and ⌈g⌉ = ε ∘ F g are mutually inverse and natural, i.e. f(p) ≤ q ⟹ p ≤ g(q) and back in the thin case

Program Definition Adjunction_to_Transform {A : F ⊣ U} : F ∹ U := {| Transformation.unit := {| transform := fun _ => unit |}; Transformation.counit := {| transform := fun _ => counit |} |}.  — direction (a) ⇒ (b): an adjunction yields η : Id ⟹ U ◯ F and ε : F ◯ U ⟹ Id with both triangle identities (obligations closed via iso_from_to / iso_to_from of adj)

Definition unit {x : D} : x ~> U (F x) := ⌊id⌋.  Definition counit {x : C} : F (U x) ~> x := ⌈id⌉.  — the book's display (1.108) itself: at a thin category the mere inhabitation of these two hom-types IS p ≤ g(f(p)) and f(g(q)) ≤ q, and the derivation is exactly the book's ('take q := f(p) and feed in reflexivity f(p) ≤ f(p)', here id transposed).  Accompanied by Corollary counit_fmap_unit (:280) ε ∘ fmap[F] η ≈ id and Corollary fmap_counit_unit (:288) fmap[U] ε ∘ η ≈ id

statement_record.book: For monotone maps f : P → Q and g : Q → P between preorders the following are equivalent: (a) f is left adjoint to g, i.e. f(p) ≤ q ⟺ p ≤ g(q) for all p, q; (b) for all p ∈ P and q ∈ Q, p ≤ g(f(p)) and f(g(q)) ≤ q (display (1.108)). Proof: (a) ⇒ (b) by feeding reflexivity into the biconditional; (b) ⇒ (a) by monotonicity of g resp. f plus transitivity.
statement_record.intree: Adjunction_from_Transform (A : F ∹ U) : F ⊣ U and Adjunction_to_Transform {A : F ⊣ U} : F ∹ U, where F ⊣ U is the hom-setoid isomorphism `adj {x y} : (F x ~> y) ≊ (x ~> U y)` with naturality in both variables (Theory/Adjunction.v:130) and F ∹ U is `Class Adjunction_Transform := { unit : Id ⟹ U ◯ F; counit : F ◯ U ⟹ Id; counit_fmap_unit : counit (F X) ∘ fmap[F] (unit X) ≈ id; fmap_counit_unit : fmap[U] (counit X) ∘ unit (U X) ≈ id }` (Adjunction/Natural/Transformation.v:35); plus `Definition unit := ⌊id⌋` / `Definition counit := ⌈id⌉` (Theory/Adjunction.v:214,215).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger as a categorification, intree-weaker as an implication in one direction. Side (a) is matched exactly: at a thin category `adj` is a bijection between the two one-element-or-empty hom-setoids, i.e. the biconditional (1.96), and its four naturality fields hold vacuously because Proset's hom-setoid is `equiv := fun _ _ => True` (Instance/Proset.v:33). Side (b) is where the strengths diverge: the book requires ONLY the two inequalities, while `F ∹ U` additionally demands that η and ε be NATURAL transformations and satisfy both triangle identities. In a preorder all four extras are automatic, so the two readings coincide there — but no in-tree lemma records that vacuity, so `Adjunction_from_Transform` is literally a proof from a stronger hypothesis than Prop 1.107(b). Conversely (a) ⇒ (b) is intree-stronger: it delivers naturality and the zig-zags, not merely the two inequalities.

gap: The equivalence exists only for functors between arbitrary categories; nothing states it for monotone maps. Precisely missing: (i) no in-tree statement writes (1.108) in order form (p ≤ g(f(p)), f(g(q)) ≤ q) — `grep -i galois` returns only prose, `GaloisConnection` 0 hits; (ii) no Functor between two Prosets is ever constructed (Instance/Proset.v's only consumers are Instance/Poset.v and Test/Poset.v), so neither side of the equivalence is instantiated at a preorder, even though `Diagonal_Product_Adjunction Props` (Adjunction/Diagonal/Product.v:36 at the thin cartesian Instance/Props.v:69) would supply such an instance with no new code; (iii) the one-line observation that makes the book's weaker (b) suffice at a thin category — Proset/Props hom-setoids identify all parallel proofs, so naturality and the triangle identities are vacuous — is nowhere recorded, so the book's exact implication '(1.108) alone gives the adjunction' is not an in-tree consequence.

statement_record.book: Let f : P → Q be left adjoint to g : Q → P. For any subset A ⊆ Q with image g(A) = {g(a) | a ∈ A}: if A has a meet in Q then g(A) has a meet in P and g(⋀A) ≅ ⋀ g(A). Dually, if A ⊆ P has a join then f(A) has a join in Q and f(⋁A) ≅ ⋁ f(A). Proof: g(⋀A) is a lower bound by monotonicity; any lower bound b of g(A) transposes to f(b) ≤ a for all a, hence f(b) ≤ ⋀A, hence b ≤ g(⋀A).
